# Building a service with only the permissive protocols module

A third-party rimsky service needs exactly one rimsky dependency: the protocols
module, which is Apache-2.0. Nothing from the rest of the product is pulled in.

## The service's module

Your service is its own Go module. Its `go.mod` requires one rimsky module:

```
require github.com/rimsky-ai/rimsky-core/lib/protocols v...
```

Build it:

```bash
go build -o service .

# and for a deployment's platform
GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o service-linux .
```

## Check the boundary yourself

```bash
go list -m all | grep '^github.com/rimsky-ai/'
# github.com/rimsky-ai/rimsky-core/lib/protocols

go list -deps . | grep '^github.com/rimsky-ai/'
# every package is under .../lib/protocols/...
```

One rimsky module, and every rimsky package linked is under it. Every Go file in
the protocols module declares Apache-2.0; the root module — which a service does not
depend on — declares AGPL. A service author integrating with rimsky does not
place their own service under copyleft.

## Run it against a deployment

Declare it as an ordinary gRPC executor:

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers: {}
named_locks: {}
executors:
  "third-party":
    transport: grpc
    endpoint: "service:9400"
    protocols: ["executor"]
```

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/executors/third-party"
```

The discovery probe's `Capabilities` call returns the service's own declared error
class — for example `third-party/refused`.

Drive two dispatches at it. One node settles fresh, carrying the service's success
delta on the record (`served_by: third-party-service`); one settles failed carrying
the service's own error class. The service's log shows both executions.

The service is a working participant, not merely a compiling one.
